lutusi-liancheng-heritage-resettlement.title: Fourteen households moved and houses pulled down for the Lutusi heritage tourism site
lutusi-liancheng-heritage-resettlement.place: Liancheng Village, Liancheng Town, Yongdeng County, Lanzhou, Gansu, China
lutusi-liancheng-heritage-resettlement.point: Liancheng Town, the town the resettlement plan names as the site of the Lutusi Ancient Government Center works. Town centre from OpenStreetMap; the completion report gives no coordinates.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Project P091949, loan IBRD-75420 of US$38.40 million for the Gansu Cultural and Natural Heritage Protection and Development Project, approved 20 March 2008, effective 11 August 2008, closed 30 June 2015 after two restructurings; US$35.02 million was disbursed. Environmental category A. Five safeguard policies were triggered: environmental assessment OP 4.01, involuntary resettlement OP 4.12, physical cultural resources OP 4.11, indigenous peoples OP 4.10 and safety of dams OP 4.37. The Bank's completion report of 27 February 2016 rates the outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory, and risk to the development outcome Moderate. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 14 January 2019 agrees on outcome, Bank performance and borrower performance, and prints the risk rating as Modest.

companies.name: Gansu Provincial Development and Reform Commission
companies.role: Implementing agency. The completion report names it as the implementing agency and places the Provincial Project Management Office inside it. No contractor is named in the documents.

lutusi-liancheng-heritage-resettlement.community: Nine sites were funded. Two of them took land and houses: the Lutusi Ancient Government Center tourism area at Liancheng and the Qingcheng Ancient Town heritage area. The Bank's completion report gives the finished figures for both together: 14 households relocated, 19.54 mu of land permanently acquired and 870.71 square metres of housing pulled down, with 26 households and 123 people affected either permanently or temporarily. All of the relocation and all of the demolition happened at Lutusi; its table shows 17 households planned against 14 actual, and 1,241.49 square metres of housing planned against 870.71 actual. The report rates the resettlement work moderately satisfactory for two reasons it names: water and electricity were slow to reach the resettlement houses at Lutusi, and the site chosen for seven households was not accepted by all of them. The refusal ended the plan for the site's car park, and the land acquisition for it was dropped. The report also says no complaint was received during the project and that compensation for land and houses was at least as high as the resettlement plans set out.
lutusi-liancheng-heritage-resettlement.outcome: The project closed on 30 June 2015. The completion report says land acquisition and resettlement cost more than twice the estimate, which it attributes to compensation rates and costs rising over the life of the project. The report's body text gives the estimate as RMB 2.76 million and the final cost as RMB 5.80 million; the actual column of its own Table A6-1 gives RMB 5.79 million, and the report does not explain the difference. It does not say when water and electricity reached the Lutusi resettlement houses. The report also gives two different planned household figures: its body text says the appraisal estimated 34 households, while the planned column of Table A6-1 gives 17. It does not reconcile them.

lutusi-liancheng-heritage-resettlement.displaced_label: 14 households relocated, from the actual column of the World Bank completion report's resettlement table
lutusi-liancheng-heritage-resettlement.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 665 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report counts 14 households relocated and 26 households with 123 people affected permanently or temporarily.
lutusi-liancheng-heritage-resettlement.confidence_note: The World Bank's own completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of that report are the only sources found. The lender is reporting on its own project. No independent press report, court record or audit of the Lutusi resettlement was found; a Chinese-language search on the township name returned nothing. The 14 households, the 19.54 mu and the 870.71 square metres sit in the actual column of the report's own table, beside the planned figures of 17 households and 1,241.49 square metres, so they are outcome figures and not the plan reprinted. The two documents give the risk rating under different words: the completion report's data sheet says Moderate and the Evaluation Group's column says Modest.

shihutang-dam-ganjiang-relocation.title: 141 households moved and 654.9 hectares taken for the Shihutang dam on the Gan River
shihutang-dam-ganjiang-relocation.place: Shihutang, Wanhe Town, Taihe County, Ji'an, Jiangxi, China
shihutang-dam-ganjiang-relocation.point: Wanhe Town, Taihe County. The resettlement plan places the complex at Shihutang natural village, Wanhe town, Taihe county. Town centre from OpenStreetMap; the Bank documents give no coordinates.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Project P101988, loan IBRD-75800 of US$100 million for the Jiangxi Shihutang Navigation and Hydropower Complex Project, approved 25 September 2008, effective 15 January 2009, restructured 15 November 2011, closed 30 June 2014; the full US$100 million was disbursed. Environmental category A. Five safeguard policies were triggered: involuntary resettlement OP 4.12, environmental assessment OP 4.01, natural habitats OP 4.04, physical cultural resources OP 4.11 and safety of dams OP 4.37. The Bank's completion report of 18 December 2014 rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory, and risk to the development outcome Low or Negligible; it rates the carrying out of the resettlement plan Moderately Satisfactory because land acquisition difficulties held up the works. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 20 April 2015 agrees on all four ratings and prints the risk rating as Negligible to Low.

companies.name: Jiangxi Administration of Navigation Affairs
companies.role: Implementing agency, the provincial body for inland waterway navigation in Jiangxi; the Jiangxi Project Management Office sat within it and ran the land acquisition and resettlement with the county governments. No construction contractor is named in the documents.

shihutang-dam-ganjiang-relocation.community: The complex is a dam, a ship lock and a hydropower station on the middle Gan River, with flood protection works. The Bank's completion report says that when it was finished the project had permanently acquired 654.9 hectares of land, against an appraisal estimate of 615 hectares, and temporarily acquired 70.6 hectares against an estimate of 330 hectares, and that 141 households comprising 515 people were relocated, against an appraisal estimate of 169 households comprising 597 people. The appraisal document says the works would affect about 53 villages and one state farm in Taihe County. The report records that some activities fell behind schedule, naming the building of the Huangkeng resettlement site and the land acquisition for the Dongmen canal in the Wanhe protection area, and that land acquisition for the Donggang diversion canal ran into difficulties that forced the engineering design to be changed. It also says special financial and physical help was given to the vulnerable households identified, that some farmland was raised to cut flooding, and that an outside agency monitored the resettlement every six months and confirmed that it met the Bank's requirements.
shihutang-dam-ganjiang-relocation.outcome: The project closed on 30 June 2014 and the ship lock was built. The completion report says the lock's full capacity will only be used by about 2020, because the Xiajiang lock downstream was finished in May 2014. The completion report's cost table carries land acquisition and resettlement on two lines, both in US dollars and both in the counterpart column with no Bank loan amount against them: US$2.13 million planned and US$2.17 million actual for the complex itself, and US$28.65 million planned and US$28.87 million actual for the flood protection works.

shihutang-dam-ganjiang-relocation.displaced_label: 141 households, 515 people relocated (World Bank completion report, 2014)
shihutang-dam-ganjiang-relocation.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 597 for this project. That is the appraisal and resettlement-plan figure for the number of people to be moved, not the outcome: the plan says "There are 597 people needed to relocate, referring to 169 households", and the completion report says 141 households comprising 515 people were relocated.
shihutang-dam-ganjiang-relocation.confidence_note: The World Bank's own completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of that report are the only sources found for the resettlement. The lender is reporting on its own project. A Chinese-language search on the dam and township names returned nothing outside the Bank. The 141 households and 515 people are the completion report's own outcome figures and differ from the plan's 169 households and 597 people, so they are not the plan reprinted. The Evaluation Group's review adds that the difficulty on the Donggang canal came from a number of households refusing the resettlement plan, but attributes that to a clarification from the Bank's project team rather than to any document, so it is not stated here as a finding. The two documents give the risk rating under different words: the completion report says Low or Negligible and the review's column says Negligible to Low.

ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.title: A Uyghur herders' village flooded and demolished for the Ertanggou reservoir
ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.place: Tuyamar village, Qialekan administrative village, Shanshan County, Turpan, Xinjiang, China
ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.point: The Ertanggou dam. The resettlement plan gives the dam's position as 89 degrees 53 minutes east and 43 degrees 18 minutes north, converted here to decimal degrees.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Project P111163, loan IBRD-79340 of US$100 million for the Xinjiang Turfan Water Conservation Project, approved 17 June 2010, effective 28 October 2010, closed 31 March 2017; the full US$100 million was disbursed. Environmental category A. Seven safeguard policies were triggered: environmental assessment OP 4.01, natural habitats OP 4.04, pest management OP 4.09, physical cultural resources OP 4.11, indigenous peoples OP 4.10, involuntary resettlement OP 4.12 and safety of dams OP 4.37. The Bank's completion report of 13 October 2017 rates the outcome Highly Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory, and risk to the development outcome Moderate. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 22 November 2017 agrees on the first four ratings and prints the risk rating as Modest.

companies.name: Turpan Prefecture Water Resources Bureau
companies.role: Implementing agency, the prefectural water authority in Xinjiang; its project management office ran the works. The resettlement itself was carried out by the Shanshan County government, which set up a project leading group and a resettlement office for it. No construction contractor is named in the documents.

ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.community: The project built three reservoirs to store water upstream: Alagou, Meiyaogou and Ertanggou. The Ertanggou reservoir flooded a hamlet called Tuyamar village, known as the Ertanggou villager group of Qialekan administrative village. The Bank's completion report says the reservoir affected 103 people in 26 households, all of them Uyghur herders, and that the whole village was inundated and the houses demolished. The report prints an inundation inventory of 4,774.36 square metres of houses, 14.11 mu of arable land, 21.37 mu of orchard, 35.05 mu of man-made pasture, 700 mu of natural pasture, 167.86 mu of forestry land, 2.5 kilometres of pasture road and one hydrological station. Every figure in that table also stands, to the decimal, in the reservoir’s 2009 resettlement plan, where the housing line reads "the area of houses which will be resettled is 4774.36 m2". The report gives the table as impact and the plan gives it as forecast, and no document says the two were measured again at the end. Four more households who lived outside the village but owned assets in it are counted inside the 103. Nobody living around the Alagou and Meiyaogou reservoirs was affected, and a few trees and other assets lost there were compensated. Shanshan County built a new site 15 kilometres away in a Uyghur neighbourhood, with 29 house yards of 1,300 square metres each, water and power, a road, a small clinic, a grocery store, a new mosque and an enlarged primary school in the next village. Each household was given a set of furniture worth RMB 5,000. For the resettlers' livelihoods, 14 hectares of desert land was reclaimed at the new site and 818 metres of irrigation canals were built; the report says the soil was highly saline at first and the households were given technical help with it. The report says their living standards were restored and improved and that they were satisfied with the compensation. A survey of 10 of the 26 households by the project's outside monitor puts average household income at RMB 41,646 in 2014 against RMB 28,175 before the move.
ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.outcome: The project closed on 31 March 2017. The completion report's cost table gives the resettlement as budgeted at 22,156.8 thousand yuan and spent at 20,229.7 thousand yuan, with the rural resettlement line itself spending more than planned and other lines less. Shanshan County added Y27.63 million of its own for housing and productive infrastructure at the new site, which the report says brought the total to Y47.86 million, double the original budget. The report says the herders had stopped pasturing with a subsidy of RMB 3,500 a person a year, and attributes that pause to a hill-closure campaign for ecological rehabilitation run by Turpan Prefecture rather than to the project. A new pasture road was built along the mountains at the herders' request.

ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.displaced_label: 26 households relocated, 103 people affected (World Bank completion report, 2017)
ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 108 for this project. The Bank's completion report counts 103 people in 26 households at Tuyamar village, says the whole village was inundated and the houses demolished, and describes their relocation to a new site 15 kilometres away. The figure 103 also appears in the project's 2009 resettlement plan, which projected "resettlers in the planning year of the project construction will reach 103 in 21 households"; the household count differs between the two documents, 21 planned against 26 in the completion report, which also records 29 house yards built.
ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.ecosystem: The reservoir flooded 700 mu of natural pasture, 35.05 mu of man-made pasture and 167.86 mu of forestry land. Those three figures are in the completion report's inundation table and also, unchanged, in the 2009 resettlement plan that forecast them. The new site was made by reclaiming 14 hectares of desert land, which the report says was highly saline at first.
ertanggou-reservoir-tuyamar-village-inun.confidence_note: The World Bank's own completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of that report are the only sources found. The lender is reporting on its own project and rates the outcome Highly Satisfactory. No independent press report, court record or field study of this village's move was found; a Chinese-language search on the reservoir and county names returned nothing about it. The report's account of the destination is favourable throughout and rests on the project's own external monitor, whose income survey covers 10 of the 26 households. The completion report's whole inundation inventory, including the 4,774.36 square metres of housing and the 103-person count, is the 2009 resettlement plan's forecast table reprinted without change, so none of those figures is an independent measurement of what was lost. What the completion report states in its own words, and the plan does not, is that the village was inundated, the houses were demolished, 26 households were resettled to a site 15 kilometres away and 29 house yards were built; the plan had forecast 20 households, rising to 21. The completion report also places Tuyamar village in Jinsheng township of Turpan city in one paragraph while the same document has Shanshan County carrying out the resettlement; it does not explain the difference. The two documents give the risk rating under different words: the report says Moderate and the review's column says Modest.

lubuk-alung-kuraitaji-road-works-death.title: Site engineer killed on the Lubuk Alung to Kuraitaji road works
lubuk-alung-kuraitaji-road-works-death.place: Lubuk Alung to Kuraitaji road, Padang Pariaman, West Sumatra, Indonesia
lubuk-alung-kuraitaji-road-works-death.point: Lubuk Alung, the northern end of the 16.23-kilometre road section the completion report names as package 21A. Village centre from OpenStreetMap; the report gives no coordinates for the spot where the engineer was hit.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Project P090990, loan IBRD-80430 for the Western Indonesia National Roads Improvement Project, approved 26 May 2011, effective 12 March 2012, closed 30 June 2021 after four restructurings. The Bank's completion report of 14 December 2021 gives the loan as US$250 million originally, revised to US$228 million, with US$224,160,404 disbursed; its cover page states the amount as SDR 145.63 million. Environmental category B, partial assessment. Three safeguard policies were triggered, per the appraisal document's own table: environmental assessment OP 4.01, physical cultural resources OP 4.11 and involuntary resettlement OP 4.12. The same table marks natural habitats OP 4.04, forests OP 4.36, indigenous peoples OP 4.10 and safety of dams OP 4.37 as not triggered. The report rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and the quality of monitoring and evaluation Substantial. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 7 June 2022 agrees on outcome and Bank performance but rates monitoring and evaluation Modest, giving shortcomings in its design as the reason. The two documents give different totals for what the project cost: the completion report's financing table gives US$224,160,404 both as the amount disbursed under the loan and as the total project cost, while the Evaluation Group's review prints US$223,780,891.76 as the total project cost and US$224,160,404.03 as the actual amount. Neither document explains the difference.

companies.name: Directorate General of Highways, Ministry of Public Works and Housing, Indonesia
companies.role: Implementing agency. The Directorate General of Highways is the national roads authority inside Indonesia's public works ministry; it ran the works through a project management unit and project implementation units in the provinces. The completion report does not name the supervision firm or the civil works contractor for package 21A.

lubuk-alung-kuraitaji-road-works-death.community: The loan paid for widening and rehabilitating national road sections along the western Sumatra corridor, and later for road repairs in Central Sulawesi. The Bank's completion report records that a fatal traffic accident happened on road package 21A on 27 July 2019, in which a site engineer working for the project's design and supervision consultants was killed. The report gives the cause as human error, a car travelling at about 60 kilometres an hour hitting him from behind while he was taking photographs in the middle of the carriageway, and says the accident "could have been prevented if adequate traffic management provisions would had been deployed". Package 21A was the 16.23-kilometre Lubuk Alung to Kuraitaji section, a second contract procured to finish works left by package 21 on the same section, which the report says was terminated in June 2019 for the contractor's poor performance. The report's table of road packages gives 21A a commencement date of 3 January 2019 and a taking-over date of 1 July 2019, which is 26 days before the accident; the report does not explain how the two fit together. On land, the report says the involuntary resettlement policy was complied with, that land acquisition and resettlement plans were prepared and published for every road package, and that all affected people were paid at replacement cost on the basis of a valuation by a firm outside the project; the rating for social safeguards was raised from Moderately Satisfactory to Satisfactory in December 2018 after early delays. Twenty-four complaints were received and resolved over the life of the project, mainly about environmental and quality shortcomings, the last of them in October 2018.
lubuk-alung-kuraitaji-road-works-death.killed_note: The one death is the site engineer killed on package 21A on 27 July 2019. The completion report gives two things as the cause in the same sentence: human error by the driver of a car that hit him from behind at about 60 kilometres an hour while he stood in the middle of the carriageway taking photographs, and the absence of adequate traffic management provisions, which the report says would have prevented it. The report says the case was handled under the Bank's environmental and social incident response procedure, that the family received the full payment due under Indonesia's work-accident insurance scheme in October 2019, that the highways directorate prepared and carried out a safeguards corrective action plan, and that the Bank closed the case with an after-action memorandum in July 2020. A payment under a work-accident scheme is not a statement of who was at fault.
lubuk-alung-kuraitaji-road-works-death.outcome: The project closed on 30 June 2021. The completion report lists package 21A as completed. The Bank formally closed the fatality case in July 2020.

lubuk-alung-kuraitaji-road-works-death.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 442 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. No World Bank document found for this project counts people or households relocated; the completion report says only that all affected people were compensated at replacement cost.
lubuk-alung-kuraitaji-road-works-death.confidence_note: The World Bank's own completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of that report are the only sources found. The lender is reporting on its own project. A search of Indonesian-language press for the 27 July 2019 accident on the Lubuk Alung to Kuraitaji works returned nothing. The engineer is not named in either document and no other injury or death is recorded. The completion report gives both a driver's error and a missing traffic management provision as the cause in one sentence, and both are set out here; whether the death is counted against the project turns on which of the two is taken as the cause, and no document settles that. Nothing in either document counts anyone relocated.

rodriguez-ecotourism-site-397-families-r.title: 397 families moved off the Rodriguez ecotourism site, some still waiting at project close
rodriguez-ecotourism-site-397-families-r.place: Rodriguez (Montalban), Rizal, Philippines, with the relocation site at Kasiglahan Village Phase 1-D, Barangay San Jose
rodriguez-ecotourism-site-397-families-r.point: Kasiglahan Village, Barangay San Jose, Rodriguez (Montalban), Rizal, the site the completion report names as where most of the families were accommodated. Point from OpenStreetMap; the documents give no coordinates for the ecotourism site itself.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Project P070899. The completion report covers the original loan and the additional financing together and gives no project number for the additional financing; the number P117470 is the one ICIJ files it under. Loan 7205-PH (IBRD-72050) of US$5 million for the Laguna de Bay Institutional Strengthening and Community Participation Project, dated 26 January 2004, approved 4 December 2003, effective 2 April 2004; additional financing of US$10 million as loan 8035-PH (IBRD-80350), approved 12 April 2011, dated 12 May 2011, effective 27 July 2011, of which US$4.5 million was cancelled on 11 July 2013 and a further US$3 million at project closing. The closing date was extended five times: four extensions totalling 27 months, to 30 April 2011, and then a fifth of three years when the additional financing became effective, to 30 April 2014, when the project closed. The Bank's completion report of 25 November 2014 gives the amount disbursed as US$6.80 million on its data sheet and US$6.83 million in its financing table. Environmental category B. The involuntary resettlement policy OP 4.12 and the indigenous peoples policy were triggered. The report rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory, borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory, the government's performance Moderately Unsatisfactory, and risk to the development outcome Substantial. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 8 October 2015 agrees on outcome, Bank performance and borrower performance, and prints the risk rating as Significant.

lenders.name: Netherlands Ministry of Foreign Affairs
lenders.role: Parallel grant TF-52826 of US$5 million at appraisal for the institutional development component, of which US$4.24 million was spent, per the completion report's financing table.

companies.name: Laguna Lake Development Authority
companies.role: Implementing agency, the national government corporation that regulates the Laguna de Bay basin; it lent project funds on to local governments, which chose and built the sub-projects.

companies.name: Municipal Government of Rodriguez, Rizal
companies.role: The local government that ran the ecotourism sub-project. The Bank's completion report says it had to relocate and resettle the 397 families and that it prepared the resettlement action plan, and that it is leading the building of the Sitio Sapo site with the National Housing Authority on land development.

rodriguez-ecotourism-site-397-families-r.community: The project lent money to local governments around Laguna de Bay for small environmental works. The Bank's completion report says one sub-project carried a relocation and resettlement requirement: "The Rodriquez LGU had to relocate and resettle 397 families of illegal settlers from their ecotourism sub-project site." Most of those families were accommodated at Kasiglahan Village Phase 1-D in Barangay San Jose. The relocation of a few families was still outstanding when the project closed, because the Sitio Sapo resettlement site had been held up over its development permit and environmental compliance certificate; the report says that site was still under construction, led by the municipality with the National Housing Authority on land development and a non-governmental organisation on social preparation and house building. The report also records one expropriation case filed over the road right of way for the Pangil materials recovery facility sub-project. The Rodriguez sub-projects appear under the additional financing in the report's own list of sub-projects. For the rest of the project the report says all land acquisition was done after securing the consent of the owners affected, through purchase, lease, donation, usufruct or exchange, and it rates compliance with the involuntary resettlement policy satisfactory. The ecotourism site also drew a claim from indigenous people that a religious ritual site of theirs lay inside it; the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples investigated, cleared the sub-project, and the municipality signed an agreement giving the indigenous group 3 per cent of the sub-project's revenue.
rodriguez-ecotourism-site-397-families-r.outcome: The project closed on 30 April 2014. The Evaluation Group's review of October 2015 lists the relocation of a few families to Sitio Sapo as one of two matters still pending at closure, the other being the Pangil expropriation case. Neither document says how many families were still waiting, and no later document was found that says whether the Sitio Sapo site was finished.

rodriguez-ecotourism-site-397-families-r.displaced_label: 397 families relocated and resettled (World Bank completion report, 2014)
rodriguez-ecotourism-site-397-families-r.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 397 for this project. Unusually for this table, the same number appears in the Bank's completion report with a relocation verb attached: it says the Rodriguez local government had to relocate and resettle 397 families from the ecotourism sub-project site, and that most of them were accommodated at Kasiglahan Village Phase 1-D.
rodriguez-ecotourism-site-397-families-r.confidence_note: The World Bank's own completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of that report are the only sources found. Both carry the 397 figure in the same words and the review repeats it from the report, so this is one account and not two. The documents do not say when the families were moved, how many were still waiting at closure, what they were paid, or whether they consented. They call them "illegal settlers", which is the documents' term for people without title. The Bank's own rating of compliance with its resettlement policy is satisfactory. Philippine reporting on flooding and conditions at Kasiglahan Village concerns families moved there from Metro Manila and does not name these 397 families, so it is not used here. Two routes to the Philippine government's own impact evaluation of this project failed: a direct download from nep.depdev.gov.ph was cut off twice by the proxy tunnel closing mid-transfer, and a fetch of the same file was refused by the site's robots rule.

chunhu-fenghua-access-road-demolition.title: Housing demolition for the Chunhu access road came to more than double the plan
chunhu-fenghua-access-road-demolition.point: Chunhu, Fenghua district of Ningbo, the town at one end of the Fenghua to Chunhu access road the completion report names. Town centre from OpenStreetMap; the Bank documents give no coordinates.

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Project P106956, loan IBRD-78490 of US$50 million for the Ningbo New Countryside Development Project, approved 25 February 2010, effective 16 July 2010, closed 31 March 2016 with no restructuring; the full US$50 million was disbursed. Environmental category B. Three safeguard policies were triggered: environmental assessment OP 4.01, safety of dams OP 4.37 and involuntary resettlement OP 4.12. The Bank's completion report of 20 October 2016 rates the outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory and risk to the development outcome Moderate. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 13 February 2017 rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, one notch lower. Its stated reason has five parts: relevance of objective High, relevance of design Substantial, achievement of the rural wastewater objective Substantial, achievement of the infrastructure objective Substantial, achievement of the objective of enhancing township management in small towns Modest, and efficiency Substantial. The review also rates Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory where the report rates it Satisfactory, and rates risk to the development outcome Substantial, naming risks it says materialised without being identified or mitigated; the report itself puts that risk at Moderate and the review's column for the report prints it as Modest. The review agrees with the report on borrower performance.

companies.name: Ningbo Municipality Development and Reform Commission
companies.role: Implementing agency. The completion report names it as the implementing agency; the Ningbo municipal project management office sat within it, with project implementation units in Fenghua, Ninghai and Yuyao counties. No construction contractor is named in the documents.

companies.name: Fenghua Investment Co., Ltd.
companies.role: The completion report names it as the project implementation unit for the Chunhu Town infrastructure development component, responsible for the design and construction of that infrastructure and for servicing the debt from asset management fees paid by Fenghua City. It is also named as the author of the June 2009 resettlement action plan for the Chunhu small town development sub-project. The Evaluation Group rates its performance Moderately Satisfactory.

chunhu-fenghua-access-road-demolition.community: The loan paid for rural wastewater treatment in 144 villages, a coastal water supply in Fenghua and town infrastructure at Chunhu, including the Fenghua to Chunhu access road. The Bank's completion report says that the permanent land acquisition and the demolition of houses both came out higher than planned. Its table in the social safeguards annex gives the finished figures against the planned ones: 325.63 mu of land permanently acquired against 265.06 planned, a rise the report puts at 24 per cent, and 7,647.6 square metres of housing demolished against 3,479 planned. All of the extra demolition is on the access road component, where 7,647.6 square metres came down against 3,027 planned; the report says the demolition doubled because of unforeseen requirements for that road, and that land first thought to need only temporary occupation had to be bought outright because it was unusable on its own once the parcels next to it had been taken. The report also says a grievance system was set up and no complaints were received over the life of the project, that all property losses were adequately compensated, and that a survey by outside monitors put the per capita net income of affected households at about RMB 58,600 in 2015 against about RMB 40,000 in 2009, with 44 per cent of affected people very satisfied with their living conditions, 50 per cent somewhat satisfied and just under 6 per cent neither satisfied nor dissatisfied.
chunhu-fenghua-access-road-demolition.outcome: The project closed on 31 March 2016. The completion report says the resettlement and the buying of the additional land were carried out satisfactorily in line with the resettlement plan, and that a post-evaluation by the National Research Center for Resettlement found the Bank's social safeguard requirements satisfactorily met. No Bank document found counts how many households lost the 7,647.6 square metres of housing.

sources.title: Ningbo Rural Development Project, Sub-project of Small Town Development of Chunhu, Fenghua: Resettlement Action Plan (evaluation version) (P106956)

chunhu-fenghua-access-road-demolition.displaced_label: 7,647.6 square metres of housing demolished and 325.63 mu of land permanently acquired, from the actual column of the World Bank completion report's resettlement table
chunhu-fenghua-access-road-demolition.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 287 for this project. That is the resettlement plan's figure: the June 2009 plan says "There are 95 households for 287 persons affected", counting people affected permanently and temporarily. No outcome document found counts people or households relocated, so no number is entered in the displaced field, which on this map holds people, households or families actually moved.
chunhu-fenghua-access-road-demolition.confidence_note: The World Bank's own completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of that report are the only sources found, and only the completion report carries the land and demolition figures. The lender is reporting on its own project and rates the resettlement satisfactory with no complaints received. No document found counts the households whose houses came down, so the harm here is the land taken and the floor area demolished, both in the actual column of the report's own table, and not a count of people. The same document gives two different totals for land acquired: the Bank's own annex table and body text give 325.63 mu, 24 per cent above the 265.06 mu planned, while the summary of the borrower's own completion report in Annex 5 gives 270.67 mu, "5.61mu more than planned". Both passages of that one report agree on 7,647.62 square metres of housing. Nothing in the report reconciles the two land figures. The same annex gives the planned area as 262 mu in its text and 265.06 mu in its table. A note on the document cache: the file harvested as this project's completion report under the name ICR_2016-10-20_26901073 is in fact the completion report for the Dominican Republic Social Protection Investment Project, Report No. ICR00003930; the figures here come from ICR_2016-10-20_26901074, which is Report No. ICR00003806 for this project.

quy-nhon-coastal-cities-sanitation-reset.note: ICIJ row P090374, VN-GEF-Coastal Cities Project, is the Global Environment Facility grant to the Coastal Cities Environmental Sanitation Project and is already on the map as quy-nhon-coastal-cities-sanitation-resettlement, which already carries the GEF grant TF094335 in its lender list. The documents harvested for this row are the same joint completion report of 2015 the existing case cites, covering P082295, P122940 and P090374, plus the appraisal document for the GEF grant and three Quy Nhon resettlement plans. Nothing in them adds a fact the existing case does not already carry: its 189.4 hectares, 1,247 affected households, 223 resettled against 245 planned, 259 land plots on five sites, VND 233 billion paid, and VND 3 billion placed in treasury accounts for 11 Quy Nhon households, are all in paragraphs 49 to 51 of that report. No extend is offered. One correction is reported rather than written into the file because fields_add cannot change a number: the existing case carries displaced: 1247, which is the completion report's count of affected households, while the report's count of households resettled is 223. Checker's addition to that correction: both figures are three-city totals. The completion report's sentence is "The project acquired around 189.4 ha of land in all three cities, with 1,247 affected HHs, of which 223 HHs had to be resettled", covering Quy Nhon, Nha Trang and Dong Hoi, and the report gives no Quy Nhon-only breakdown of either number. So 223 should not simply replace 1,247 on a card named for Quy Nhon; whichever number is carried, the label has to say it is the three-city total.

ningbo-solid-waste-recycling.drop_reason: The only relocation count anywhere in this project's documents exists solely as something Bank staff told the Bank's evaluators. The Evaluation Group's review of 3 June 2021 says: "The project team provided following information on land acquisition: the actual resettlement impacts included 650 mu (43 ha) of permanent land acquisition with impact on 478 farmers' and 370 workers' livelihood, and relocation of 167 households with 395 persons, among which 51 households moved into their replacement apartments and 116 households got cash compensation." The same review says plainly, in the sentence above it, "The ICR does not discuss the magnitude of land acquisition." Checked in the outcome document: the completion report of 9 December 2020, paragraph 80, is the project's only account of what happened, and it gives no relocation figure at all - "According to the final external resettlement monitoring report for the project, there were 1,249 project affected persons due to construction of the transfer stations, the KWTF, the Ningbo municipal waste disposal center and Reconstruction of Dongqiao Town Xuanpei Village" - and then records that "as of the time of this ICR, all land acquisition and resettlement related compensatory activities have been completed in full". Paragraph 82 says complaints received were recorded and addressed properly. A count of people affected is not a count of people moved, and the review's own account of the outside monitor's June 2020 report is that the resettlement was fully completed, incomes and housing fully restored, with no pending issue or complaint. The 683 persons, 5,360 square metres of houses and 55,300 square metres of business buildings that the review prints are the 2012 resettlement plan's figures in the future tense, attributed by the review itself to the appraisal document. The review also states that Dongqiao Town was demolished for the kitchen waste facility and had to be rebuilt at a new site, but attributes that too to the project team's clarification rather than to a document. Neither limb of the forward rule is met on any document.

china-renewable-energy-scale-up-cresp.drop_reason: No outcome document counts anyone relocated, and both outcome documents record the opposite of harm. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 24 June 2012 says "Land acquisition and resettlement for all investment projects have been satisfactorily implemented. All compensation have been paid to the affected people based on the Resettlement Action Plan (RAP), all relocated households have completed the construction of replacement houses, and all proposed rehabilitation measures indicated in the RAP have been implemented for the affected villages. Income and livelihood of the affected people have been restored and even increased compared with that before resettlement." It gives no count with that sentence. The two problems it names are a change of site for the Rudong biomass plant, resolved by the owners leasing rather than selling the fuel storage land, and a revised land acquisition estimate for access roads in Inner Mongolia, resolved by an updated plan approved by the Bank. The field-based Project Performance Assessment Report of 30 June 2017, paragraph 3.21, says "The project encountered no significant issues with land acquisition and resettlement for the pilot-investment subprojects" and that the Inner Mongolia issues were satisfactorily addressed during supervision. ICIJ's 570 traces to the appraisal document and the 2004 resettlement plans, which count 31 households with 147 people affected at the Pingtan wind farm, "with none needing relocation", and 25 households with 103 people at the Rudong plant site. Those are plan figures in the future tense for impacts the two outcome documents say caused no issue. Neither limb of the forward rule is met.

china-cresp-phase-one-follow-up.drop_reason: This row is the second IBRD loan of the same programme as P067828, not a Global Environment Facility grant; the assessment report describes it as "a second IBRD loan (P096158) to finance two additional pilot investments". The completion report of 24 June 2012 covers both loans and the GEF grant together, so the two rows share outcome documents. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 24 June 2012 and the field-based Project Performance Assessment Report of 30 June 2017, both of which cover this number, count nobody relocated and record no harm, saying compensation was fully paid, replacement houses completed, incomes restored or increased, and no significant land acquisition or resettlement issues. ICIJ's 131 traces to the resettlement action plan for the Huitengxile wind farm and the resettlement policy framework, both plans. Neither limb of the forward rule is met.

china-thermal-power-efficiency.drop_reason: ICIJ's 702 is a resettlement plan's affected-population count for a heat supply pipeline, and no outcome document carries it or anything like it. The October 2007 plan for the Shandong Huangtai power plant heat supply pipe network says "the actually affected population is 225 households with 702 persons (in which 146 households with 462 persons are affected by land acquisition, 53 households with 163 persons are affected by relocation and 26 households with 77 persons are affected by both land requisition and relocation)" - a survey of expected impacts, in a plan. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 25 February 2015, paragraph 46, is the project's only account of social safeguards and it is about workers, not land: "The implementation of involuntary resettlement was rated satisfactory as the approved Resettlement Plan Framework and resettlement plans associated with the nine closed small power plants had been followed... Adequate compensation and social protection measures for settlement of affected workers were provided. The post evaluation activity did not identify any remaining social issues." The Evaluation Group's review of 9 June 2015 repeats this. The field-based Project Performance Assessment Report of 13 June 2018, paragraph 2.14, says "This ensured that most workers did not need to relocate as there were similar opportunities nearby", and its summary of what did not work says the team had underestimated the government's commitment to compensatory measures, so the funds set aside to facilitate the closures were not needed. No outcome document counts anyone relocated or records a loss. Neither limb of the forward rule is met.

laos-road-sector-project.drop_reason: No outcome document counts anyone relocated, and the only grievance either records is about road signage. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 27 March 2018, paragraph 64, says "Project implementation was in line with the social safeguards frameworks and plans, and there were no reports of major social safeguards issues in the progress reports (only minor issues about traffic control during construction, which were addressed by the contractors and project manager)". Its borrower section, item A.1.c, says "All resettlements on NR1B and NR6A were fully paid by GoL in accordance with Law and Regulations prior to the start of constructions." Its mission record says "The RAP implementation has been completed with compensation and required support provided to all Project Affected Households (PAH)... The PAHs met confirmed the receipt of cash compensation from the Project", and that the grievances raised were "mainly related to the need for further improvement of road safety measures such as traffic control sign posts at some points of the NR6A". ICIJ's 399 traces to the 2008 and 2009 resettlement plans and ethnic group development plans for roads 1B and 6A, which project 24 households to be relocated, 1,109 square metres of structures to be demolished and 26 households affected, all in the future tense. The candidate sentences flagged as deaths in the pre-extracted brief are road-safety indicators and a plan's list of future risks, not deaths. One conflict is left unreconciled: the Evaluation Group's review of 24 May 2018 says "The ICR author advised there were no persons affected by the project", while the completion report itself describes compensation paid to project-affected households on both roads. Neither limb of the forward rule is met on any document.

vietnam-central-north-health-support.drop_reason: No outcome document counts anyone relocated or records a loss. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 24 February 2017, paragraph 49, says the involuntary resettlement policy was triggered because the project built preventive health centres where no health facility had stood before, that "The activities implemented, including the assessment of socioeconomic impacts, reimbursement of losses, and recovery of income, were carefully prepared and fully implemented", and that the mid-term review report "confirmed the construction of 30 DPHCs with no complaints on compensation/resettlement". The Evaluation Group's review of 23 June 2017 repeats this and finds full compliance with the safeguard policies. ICIJ's 366 traces to the November 2009 resettlement policy framework, which says "There are 98 housholds impacted by the project. However, no residential land will be acquired" and lists land to be taken by district, mostly public vacant land. That framework also carries a null sentence - "acquisition of any private land for construction of district care centers will not be necessary and OP 4.12 on Involuntary Resettlement will not be triggered by any component under the project" - which is noted here as evidence and is not what decided this drop; the two outcome documents are. Neither limb of the forward rule is met.

vietnam-urban-water-supply-development.drop_reason: The compensation delay this project records has its consequence named in the same paragraph, and the consequence is to the works. Checked in the outcome documents: the completion report of 12 December 2013, section 2.4, says "Land acquisition was carried out following the provision stipulated in the RAPs and the RPF. The project complied with social safeguard policies. However, the project experienced substantial delays in the implementation of site clearances and compensation... These delays had considerable adverse impact on the progress of civil works, particularly for subprojects in Hanoi, Thai Nguyen, Bac Ninh and Ha Tinh." Section 2.1 gives three causes of the delay: late mobilisation of government counterpart funding for compensation, disagreement between district committees and affected persons over the amount of compensation, and weak collaboration between the provincial project management units and the district committees. The Evaluation Group's review of 12 December 2015 repeats the same sentences and the same stated consequence. Neither document counts a household, names a site, says any compensation went unpaid or below replacement cost, or says any livelihood was not restored. The harm named is to the progress of the civil works. ICIJ's 360 traces to the November 2008 resettlement plan, which counts 79 households affected by agricultural land acquisition in four sub-projects in Hai Duong province, and to the appraisal document of 22 November 2004, which says "No household will be relocated and assets affected are mainly agricultural land, trees and crops." Neither limb of the forward rule is met.

gef-ningbo-water-and-environment.drop_reason: The component that would have displaced people was never carried out, and the completion report says so in terms. Checked in the outcome document: the completion report of 18 May 2012, section 2.4, says "Since the restoration of the mudflats in Plots A3 and A5 did not take place, those engaged in aquaculture were not displaced and their livelihoods were not affected by the project. Therefore, there was no need to implement the RAP as envisaged. Consultation activities envisaged in the RAP were, however, carried out and fishermen were offered compensation on a voluntary basis. Forty-eight fishmen, including 10 women have been employed at the Wetlands Center as wage laborers. Nevertheless, this compensation scheme has not had any impact on reducing fishing activity in the area." Section 2.2 says the inter-tidal mudflats were not restored, that fish harvesting in the area in fact increased and the number of fishermen rose significantly since appraisal, and that "A resettlement action plan was prepared early in the project to identify those harvesting fishery resources from the project area along with measures for restoring their livelihoods, but it was not carried out." ICIJ's 348 traces to the April 2006 resettlement plan, which projects 114 households with 348 persons affected in Andong and Zhouxiang towns and 2,508.3 mu of aquaculture area affected - a plan for a component that did not happen. The project's shortfall here is a conservation measure not delivered, not a displacement. Neither limb of the forward rule is met.
